uncited: This family defines the memory layout, pointer encoding, and traversal logic for hierarchical acceleration structures (primarily octrees) used in volume rendering.
It solves the problem of efficiently navigating sparse 3D data by mapping tree topology to linear memory or GPU textures, enabling fast empty-space skipping and neighbor-based boundary crossing.

It differs from sibling methods by focusing on the low-level representation of the tree hierarchy itself (e.g., texture encoding, point storage) rather than high-level traversal optimizations or specific acceleration heuristics.
The traversal begins at the root of the octree and determines which of the eight children (octants) the ray intersects.
A hybrid CPU-GPU traversal strategy where the CPU traverses the KD-tree of AMR patches back-to-front, and the GPU traverses cells within a patch.
A simple binary tree indexing scheme to identify and organize patches in a breadth-first manner (coarse to fine).
Allows quick identification of cousin patches.
